dedupe_keys.name: ognet oil refinery aerial imagery dataset and detection model stanford ml group

description: OGNet is a deep learning model and dataset for detecting oil and gas infrastructure in aerial imagery, published by the Stanford ML Group with co-authors from other institutions in a paper submitted to arXiv on 14 November 2020. The project page read on 2026-09-26 says the curated dataset holds 7,066 aerial images, 149 of oil refineries and 6,917 negative images of visually similar objects and landscapes, taken from National Agriculture Imagery Program imagery of 2015 to 2019 at a minimum resolution of 1 metre over the continental United States and processed with the Descartes Labs platform. The model outputs a probability that an image contains a facility, with a threshold chosen for a precision of 0.81 at full recall on validation data, and was run over the continental US to find refineries. The dataset is a free download under the CC BY 4.0 licence. Coverage is the continental United States. Caveats: only refineries are labelled, the positive class is small, and the work is a research release that has not been updated. Simulation uses are building and checking inventories of oil facilities from imagery, which feed hazard exposure studies and methane source attribution. Related records: data-ogim-oil-gas-infrastructure-mapping and data-netl-gogi-global-oil-gas-features-database are facility inventories such detections can extend.
